title: Alert Maps and SLO Scenario Simulator — console prototype for rapid triage and rollout previews
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
High-level: Prototype a compact Alert Map panel and SLO Scenario Simulator inside the Redwood Console. The goal is to help on-call engineers and incident commanders quickly understand affected surfaces, simulated SLO impact for different escalation/rollout choices, and preview fallback behaviors before executing a rollout. This ticket contains the design artifact, synthesis of rounds of stakeholder feedback, and an initial usability testing plan.

Scope: (1) Alert Map tile that visually groups impacted routes/models by service, region, and severity with quick actions (snooze, reroute, create postmortem link). (2) SLO Scenario Simulator modal that accepts a proposed rollout (canary percent, model variant fallback, region failover) and shows projected SLO trajectory and cost delta over a 24h window. (3) Compact on-call handoff card that ships with the alert map and includes one-click links to postmortems, recent alerts, and the runbook excerpt.

Why this work: Operators struggle to reason about downstream SLO risk when changing routing/rollouts. Current alerts list is too flat; teams flip between console pages and runbooks. This prototype reduces context switching by putting causal surface and simulated outcomes adjacent to the alert thread.
acceptance_criteria: Alert Map tile renders grouped list of affected services with color-encoded severity and filters by region and model
Simulator accepts rollout parameters (canary %, duration, fallback variant, region restrictions) and returns a projected SLO curve and estimated token cost delta
One-click actions visible: open runbook excerpt, start postmortem draft, link to PR for rollback or model pin
Prototype usability test (n=6 engineers/on-call rotation members) shows median time-to-action reduced by >=20% compared to baseline workflow
Design handed off to Eng with component specs, animation frames, and accessibility annotations
design_decisions: Compact summary + expand pattern: Alert Map shows condensed grouping by default, with an expand-to-inspect flyout to prevent cluttering the main alert thread
Simulator uses discrete bucketing of SLO breach likelihood rather than noisy continuous prediction to set operator expectations and avoid overconfidence
Cost delta shown as relative percentage and absolute tokens; exact currency estimates are left to billing consoles to avoid double accounting
On-call card includes only the top 3 immediate actions to keep handoff friction low (open runbook, start postmortem, escalate to PD)
Animations for rollout preview kept minimal (fade + line chart) to maintain performance during heavy alert storms
tradeoffs: Choosing simplified SLO model (short-window exponential smoothing) reduces accuracy for long-tail scenarios but keeps compute cost low in the UI path
Including cost estimates in-situ improves decision speed but risks duplication vs billing; we mitigate by linking to canonical cost view and labeling estimates as 'preview only'
Aggressive grouping on Alert Map reduces noise but may hide low-priority signals; added filter toggle to reveal all items
Simulator runs are best-effort and not a replacement for full chaos testing — we will surface that in the UI copy
